# M1 bench arm: purchase readiness (generated by `python -m rnd.m1_readiness`)

**Kit ([M1_BENCH_ARM.md](M1_BENCH_ARM.md)), with 15% contingency:** Step 1a **$970** (buy now; measuring tools $95 of it; the W17a rig's stand, stock, mandrel and fasteners in it); Step 1b **$2,060** (after the gate; test instruments $1,197 of it: $863 if the owner has them; the rig's levers, discs, stops, guard and interlock in it); optional G-SB review service outside every total: route A $400–1,200 ESTIMATE, route B $0; Step 2 **$1,566** (today's plan: GIM6010 at pitch + elbow, inline roll); whole kit $4,596. Hold A (D20 with its drive parts) +$133; belt-roll fallback −$335; roll latch option +$16 per arm (not in a total).

## Go / no-go per step

### Step 0: free — **do now**

1. **Read the public GIM6010-8 manual** (SteadyWin rev 1: the first source under GIM6010-8 in `rnd/specs/actuators.yaml`, https://sdalal1.github.io/assets/pdf/SteadyWin_GIM6010-8_Manual_rev1.pdf). Look for: the CAN frame formats and whether MIT / impedance mode is the default, the CAN-command timeout, a torque / current limit saved to flash, the node-ID setting, the output bolt circle and the output bearing. Write what it says into docs/sw/gim_protocol_notes.md; anything it settles comes off the discovery list.
2. **Send the six seller questions below as one message** (SteadyWin reseller), and the DM-J4310 bearing question to Damiao. Answers to 5 and 6 can change 1a (a different driver version, a different output pattern); the rest gate 1b and Step 2.

### Step 1a: GIM6010-8 + DM-J4310 + CAN + 10 A CC supply + rig stand + tilt tools + lever stock + coupon parts ($970) — **GO**
- It answers the one question everything else hangs on (the SDC104 protocol) on a bare, unloaded motor at a 1 A limit, which needs no safety board (Fable #2 verdict). Every line except the supply, the rig (stand, plate stock, tilt mandrel, optical lever, fasteners), the lever stock and the measuring and coupon tools is reused in the arm.
- **No weight on the lever and no lever on the motor** until the 1b rig is built (Fable #2 C1): 1a runs with only the hub and the 12 g index disc on the output; the tilt test (1a-11) loads the tilt mandrel to 200 N radial with the motor unpowered and unplugged.
- The 1 A limit and the supply's output switch are the safety for 1a: discovery's `--enable` sends only zero-gain frames; the impedance check uses low gains at that limit.

**Step 1a exit criterion:** `sw.rig_1a` all phases pass on the GIM and the DM; GIM tilt stiffness measured and decided (docs/M1_RIG.md §3: 1a-2 … 1a-10 on the GIM, 1a-5 … 1a-9 on the DM; 1a-11 k_t ≤ 8 kN·m/rad keeps the D26 6001 support, ≥ 75 → the overhung pinion, in between the lead re-runs the split).

**Step 1a exit = the gate to buy Step 1b (all four):**
1. **Discovery done** (1a): `python -m sw.gim_discover` on the bare GIM6010-8 at 1 A answers an MIT / impedance mode; enable, zero-gain and a low-gain impedance hold work on the unloaded output; the drive's **CAN timeout** disables it when frames stop; a **torque limit saved to flash** reads back after a power cycle (or the manual / vendor tool names the registers). If there is no impedance mode, no CAN timeout or no flash limit: do not buy 1b; redesign the safety argument first (the board's timing budget is part of it).
2. **Board drawn and reviewed with the logic race fixed** (electrical track, Fable #2 M2). **Race fixed on paper in netlist v4 (W17b):** the RUN latch U28 makes K2_DRIVE = LATCH ∧ ¬RUN ∧ ¬PRE_TIMEOUT, so an uncommanded K1 drop-out fires FORCE on its own edge (coil unplugged: far end < 10 V in 2.0 ms vs T7's 4 ms); AUX is debounced by U29 (t_stable 2.1–5.7 ms); the discrepancy window is 40 ms; the U10 terms are unified. **Still open:** the KiCad schematic in the tree, and the review gate G-SB (docs/rnd/safety_board_tests.md): route A a hired EE (≈ $400–1,200, the optional service line) or route B two qualified community reviewers ($0); the owner picks the route and the person.
3. **Rig designed: delivered in W17a** (docs/M1_RIG.md, rnd/parts/rig.py, sw/config/rig_step1.yaml; Fable #2 C1): `--rig step1` in the software (ratio 1.0, rated 5 / peak 11 N·m, software range −10° … +90°, the weighed lever as the gravity model); natural-rubber stops at −15° (reference) and +100° at the centre of percussion; steel discs bolted through the bar at 0.27 m; an interlocked 3 mm polycarbonate guard ≥ 40 mm clear of every swept part; soak 4 / 2 discs (RMS 55 / 57 % of rated, band 45–65 %); rig rehearsals pass. Its parts are the 1a / 1b rig lines below.
4. **C14 measured** (1a, docs/COUPONS.md): the GIM output's tilt stiffness, bearing layout, PCD and pilot. Only then is the integral pinion quoted, as drawn (hinged output) or as the overhung variant (moment-rigid output; rnd/belts.py STUB_SUPPORT_RULE).

### Step 1b: SE-1000-24 + safety board + test kit + rig parts + pinion ($2,060) — **NO-GO until the gate**
- The board parts are ordered after the KiCad schematic and the G-SB review (the logic race is fixed in netlist v4, W17b); the board passes T0–T16 with no motor (docs/rnd/safety_board_tests.md) before any drive is powered from it.
- **Service (optional, not in the $2,060):** **Review gate G-SB, route A: hired EE review** of the safety-board KiCad schematic + layout, fixed scope (the whole checklist, the logic as a state machine with the v4 race fix, the power stage, the T0–T16 limits, a written verdict; docs/rnd/safety_board_tests.md *Review gate G-SB*) $400–1,200 (ESTIMATE (W17b: 4–8 h of a degree-level power-electronics EE)); 1b gate 2: before any 1b board part is ordered. **Route B: two qualified maker-community reviewers, $0** (or a small honorarium), 2–4 weeks instead of 1–2. The owner chooses the route and the person (W17b).
- Astra review #3 (critical 3) simulation stays the basis: as drawn the clamp rang at MHz (filter + 50 µs minimum on-time; on 26.0 / off 25.7 V), the coil driver was a 30 V part seeing ≈ 52 V, a stuck AUX bypassed pre-charge, a welded K1 / broken AUX went undetected, a dead 12 V left K1 closed with no clamp, and the 20 A fuse left the in-arm 16 AWG unprotected at 18–35 A (netlist v3 fixes all six).

**Step 1b exit criteria (all needed before Step 2 is bought):**
1. **Gate before any drive is powered from the board:** the review gate G-SB closed (docs/rnd/safety_board_tests.md: route A a hired EE or route B two qualified community reviewers, never the drafter; the checklist signed and the five pieces of evidence filed), then the board built and **every motorless test T0–T16 passed** (bench supply + dummy capacitor bank + resistor bank + CC regen source, scope at the board, at the drive end and on the drains with ×10 probes and ground springs; pass/fail numbers from rnd/safety_board_sim.py): ARM refused with a mushroom pressed, without a heartbeat or with AUX stuck; pre-charge then K1; the 10 Ω dummy load trips the pre-charge timeout; FORCE on every opening, including a K1 coil opened by unplugging (the logic race fixed, T7), never during pre-charge; WD_OK low 22.5–30 ms after the last edge and last edge → drive-end bus < 10 V ≤ 50 ms (scope, not software timestamps); no self re-arm; disarmed after a supply cycle; clamp on at 26.0 V ± 1 %, no MHz bursts, drain ≤ 48 V, drive end ≤ 27.5 V at the regen limit; loss of the 12 V, broken / stuck AUX and a linked-out K1 each end in a stop.
2. The GIM table in sw/drivers/gim.py is filled from 1a (`python -m sw.drivers.gim`: no TODO).
3. `python -m sw.bringup --rig step1 --load bringup --joints yaw,wpitch` on the W17a rig (ratio 1.0, −10° … +90°; docs/M1_RIG.md §4) passes enumerate (map, ratio 1.0, load confirmed), limits (torque limit in flash, read back, kept over a power cycle), safety (e-stop → no torque ≤ 50 ms measured, watchdog, the drive's own CAN timeout), calibrate (against the −15° reference stop, span to +100° ± 2 %), jog, gravity (the weighed lever, residual ≤ 20 % of rated), the sag test and sysid. First loaded enable (1b-1) with the bar and carrier only, the 10 A supply at 2 A and the 1a drive limit (Fable #2 C1).
4. The real loop's longest heartbeat gap (bring-up report) is under half the 25 ms watchdog, **on the Pi, with the cores loaded as on the robot** (a UVC camera streaming + `stress-ng` at ≈ 75 % CPU; Neon #2 assumption 5). If it is not: run the loop SCHED_FIFO on an isolated core, or move the heartbeat + supervisor out of Python (sw track); raising `watchdog_s` is allowed only up to 28 ms (the SW2 budget, electrical.md).
5. Torque constant from the weighed lever (`kt_method: absolute`: the ± sweeps against the lever's gravity, every part weighed to ±1 g, radii from CAD) and friction measured on the rig; the motor case temperature logged for 30 min at rated torque (1b-3).
6. **Coupons C12–C14 pass** ([COUPONS.md](COUPONS.md), pass numbers from the repo's load cases): C12 insert pull-out (M3 (Ø4.0 × 4.0 and × 6): mean ≥ 1.0 kN, lowest of 3 ≥ 0.8 kN; M4 (Ø5.6 × 5.7 and × 8): mean ≥ 1.5 kN, lowest ≥ 1.2 kN); C13 the bolted 4-ear flange (no slip at 16.5 N·m fresh and 13 N·m after 72 h at 50 °C, no tipping gap at 16.1 N·m); C14 the drive stub (the output's tilt stiffness read in 1a; the 8 × M3 × 6 + Loctite 243 joint holds 16.5 N·m with the 360 N side load on the dummy output, and the drive's 11 N·m peak on the real output on the rig).
7. **Soak test** (determinism; Asimov sim2real lesson 1, hour 20 = hour 1): `python -m sw.soak --rig step1 --load soak --joints yaw,wpitch --hours 2` passes on the rig: **soak discs 4 / 2 at 0.27 m, RMS 45–65 % of rated** (sized 55 / 57 %; Fable #2 C1: the old 2 kg at 0.3 m was 118 % of the bare motor's rated). That is a sysid fit (friction, torque constant, backlash, latency) before and after 2 h of cyclic motion, with drift ≤ 20 % Coulomb, ≤ 25 % viscous, ≤ 5 % torque constant, ≤ +0.1° backlash, ≤ +0.5 ms mean / +2 ms p95 latency; no supervisor stop, no bus-off, no new throttle flag, zero corrupted CAN frames, loop jitter p99 < 1 ms on the Pi (PREEMPT_RT reported). **Open (Fable #2 minor, lead to decide before 1b):** whether jitter p99 < 1 ms in Python over USB-CAN blocks Step 2 (proposal: report it; criterion 4 is the blocking timing number).

### Step 2: the rest of the arm — **NO-GO today**; GO when
- Step 1b's exit criteria are met (if the SDC104 has no impedance mode: stop and redesign the GIM joints' safety argument first);
- the seller has answered: the GIM8108-36's output face, bearing rating, backlash and the **SDC303 protocol** (same as the SDC104?); for hold A, the GIM8108-8's 24 V figures;
- the arm's load chain is drawn (Fable #2 M5): every joint between the shoulder and the hand has a row in joints.md (upper bone ↔ yaw flange screws, the detach clamp, the elbow core / clamp, the wrist output bearing), and the R14 (c) driver rule vs the 3 mm hex key is settled (C3);
- for hold A: the seller's 24 V answer (the D20 parts list: C45+QT pinions with 10.9 screws, PU steel-cord belts; D26);
- for the ≤ 1 mm accuracy claim: the RP2040 node firmware (the encoder mounts are drawn; M3), else M1 proves everything but accuracy.

## Day-1 plan

**Step 0 (before buying):** read the GIM6010-8 manual; send the six seller questions (below).

**Step 1a (on arrival):**
1. **Check and measure, unpowered:** the 24 V SDC104 version and the DM-J4310 V1.1; bolt the motor to the stand; C9 disc on both faces (PCDs); 1a-0 calipers (pilot, thread depth, housing pattern and which face carries it); drill the rig's motor plates and hubs to them.
2. **Protocol discovery on the bare GIM6010-8** (alone on can0, the output bare with the C9 / C14 fixtures off, the 10 A supply at 24.0 V / 1 A): vendor tool over USB-C first (node ID, firmware, 1 Mbit/s, MIT mode if offered), then `python -m sw.gim_discover --bus socketcan:can0 --id <n>` and, if the probe answers, `--enable` (zero gains, turn the output by hand). Then a low-gain impedance hold, the CAN timeout (stop sending: the drive must disable) and the flash limit (set, power-cycle, read back). Fill sw/drivers/gim.py; record what is still unknown (docs/sw/gim_protocol_notes.md).
3. **IDs and buses:** DM-J4310 ESC_ID 0x05 / MST_ID 0x15 on the same bus; the GIM6010-8 as the yaw (0x03 / 0x13, can_map.yaml); terminations: adapter jumper on, far end terminated; the CAN HAT against the two adapters (docs/sw/can_interface_note.md).
4. **The rest of 1a on the rig stand** (docs/M1_RIG.md §3; DM-J4310 first): `python -m sw.rig_1a --bus socketcan:can0 --joint <j> limits / verify / impedance / timeout / stall`, the encoder zero over a power cycle (1a-10), then 1a-11: the GIM's tilt stiffness on the tilt mandrel (unpowered; two 0.01 mm indicators, the 0.002 mm DTI on the housing, the optical lever) and the decision it gives.
5. **Coupons on the bench:** print and test C12 (insert pull-out), C13 (4-ear flange: proof, μ, tipping, then the 72 h hold) and C14 (b) (the 8 × M3 joint on the dummy output); record the results in COUPONS.md.
6. **Gate review:** discovery and 1a-11 in; the board drawn in KiCad and G-SB closed (the owner picks the route); the rig is designed (W17a) → the owner decides on 1b.

**Step 1b (after the gate):** build the board and run T0–T16 with no motor; build the rig (stops, discs, guard with its interlock in series with the mushrooms; 1b-0 bumper check); 1b-1 on the 10 A supply at 2 A, then the SE-1000-24 at 24.0 V; `python -m sw.bringup --rig step1 --load bringup --bus socketcan:can0,can1 --estop gpiod:gpiochip0:17:27 --joints yaw,wpitch`, each step gated on the one before: enumerate → limits → safety (e-stop ≤ 50 ms, watchdog 25 ms, drive CAN timeout) → calibrate (−15° reference, span to +100°) → jog → gravity → sag → sysid; then 30 min at rated torque with the case logged, a collision trip, C14 (c), and the soak (`--load soak`: guard off, discs 4 / 2 on, guard on).

Rehearse first: `python -m sw.gim_discover --bus virtual --enable`, `python -m sw.rig_1a --bus virtual`, `python -m sw.rehearse_step1` and `python -m sw.soak --rig step1 --bus virtual` (sw/test_s2.py).

## Seller questions (copy of M1_BENCH_ARM.md)

1. **GIM8108-8, 24 V:** we run a 24 V bus (6S Li-ion, 25.2 V full; our regen clamp switches on at 26.0 V ± 1 % and off at 25.7 V, and the drive end stays ≤ 27.5 V at our regen limit; please confirm the drive's absolute maximum input voltage). Which driver version of the GIM8108-8 (SDC104, GDZ468, GDS68?) do you ship, and is it specified for 24 V? Please give rated torque, rated speed, no-load speed and continuous current at 24 V (listings quote 48 V). Price and lead time for 2 now (4 later).
2. **GIM8108-8 drawing:** installation drawing with frame diameter and height, output-flange bolt pattern (hole count, PCD, thread, depth) and housing / rear mounting pattern, and the connector position.
3. **GIM8108-36 (SDC303, 24 V):** which face is the output; the output flange material and the dowel-hole depth; reducer **backlash** (listings say 15 arcmin: measured how?); frame and connector position (we have the Ø96 × 57 drawing).
4. **GIM8108-36 output bearing:** please give the **bearing type** (deep-groove, angular-contact pair, crossed-roller?) and its **radial, axial and tilting-moment ratings** (static and dynamic, and where along the output they are referenced). Our two load cases at the output flange (rnd/joints.py, M1 roll support, Astra review): **with our rear 61806 support, ≈ 1,413 N radial in service and 3,130 N radial at a fault** (a collision or a stall, including misalignment); **without it, a tilting moment of 36.4 N·m in service and 137 N·m at a fault**. One listing gives 1000 N radial / 250 N axial: please confirm, and say which of the two cases the bearing carries. Price with the SDC303 driver and lead time.
5. **CAN protocol manual** for the SDC104 (GIM6010-8), SDC303 (GIM8108-36) and the GIM8108-8's driver: frame formats; is the MIT / impedance mode (position, velocity, kp, kd, torque feed-forward) the default or selected in the tool, and its float ranges; how to set the node ID and the feedback ID; 1 Mbit/s; a **CAN-command timeout** (the drive disables itself when commands stop) and its unit; a torque / current-limit parameter **saved to flash**; encoder zero (is the output angle kept over a power cycle?); status and error codes; under/over-voltage behaviour. **Is it the same protocol on all three drivers?**
6. **GIM6010-8:** confirm the unit is the 24 V **SDC104** version (not a 48 V listing), with its installation drawing and which face carries the housing mounting holes (rear or output face: our cartridge cap depends on it, Fable C3); the output flange's bolt circle, pilot diameter and thread depth; and the **output bearing** (single deep-groove row, angular-contact pair or crossed roller?) with its radial and tilting-moment ratings (our pinion is supported by it and a second bearing, Fable #2 M3).
